title: Cost surgery: Hosting options & unit-econ deep-dive — Aurora Therapeutics
summary: Discovery focused on per-token unit economics and hosting mix. Customer has strict budget for pilot, wants guidance on batching/caching, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and security constraints for PHI-like telemetry. Agreed next steps: pricing sheet, pilot scope spreadsheet, and a bench run using a redacted sample workload.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-08 16:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Mehta (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM) -- Dr. Naveen Patel (CTO), Ethan Rivera (Head of ML), Sara Bloom (Platform Eng), Olivia Yang (Finance)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Liam, AE on the medtech vertical at Redwood. Priya is our solutions engineer, she'll drive the perf questions. Maya is here for success.
[00:09] Dr. Patel: Hi, thanks. we're on a tight budget and timeline, want to understand when dedicated vs hosted makes sense, costs per inference and where batching/caching help. also we have some telemetry that might be PHI-adjacent, so residency and KMS are important.
[00:27] Priya: Great, thanks. to be clear — when you say "per inference" are you thinking per-token or "per-response"? those differ a bit, but most of our pricing discussion centers on per-token plus embedding units for vector stuff.
[00:39] Ethan: Per-token mostly, for our chat summarization flows and structured output. typical request is 300 tokens in, 120 tokens out. QPS varies; baseline 5 qps, burst to 60 during batch uploads.
[00:56] Olivia: From finance side, pilot budget is strict — $6k for first month ideally, can stretch to $10k if we see clear runway.
[01:05] Priya: Ok, that's helpful. two levers to hit that budget: 1) hosting mix — hosted API (fastest to start) vs dedicated reserved capacity (predictable unit cost) vs private (VPC/on-prem) which adds fixed platform licensing. 2) runtime levers — batching and KV prefix caching reduce per-token compute; quantized model variants can drop cost but may have small quality delta.
[01:28] Sara: Quick Q — our model is a fine-tuned open checkpoint, does Redwood require we ship weights or can we use a model in your catalog?
[01:36] Liam: You can do both. hosted uses our catalog or bring-your-own model with private deployments. for dedicated, we can host your model and pin versions. note: private deployments give you full model custody but add set-up and licensing.
[01:49] Ethan: Can you give rough numbers — say using a 7B quantized variant, 420 tokens per round trip, what per-token are we looking at in hosted vs dedicated?
[01:59] Priya: Rough back-of-envelope: hosted for a quantized 7B-ish model, raw per-token cost might be X cents — sorry quoting hypotheticals — let's say $0.0008/token for generation in hosted on our catalog; dedicated reserved capacity can push that down depending on committed throughput, maybe 30–50% lower if you're filling racks. but remember network egress, storage, and embedding units add. caching can drop effective tokens billed: prefix/KV caching can shave 20–60% for repeated contexts.
[02:29] Dr. Patel: That delta matters. Our main question: can we start hosted while optimizing to a dedicated path if successful? and what is the operational pain moving between?
[02:39] Priya: Yes, that's the typical path. we support canary/rollout with automatic routing. movement is mostly config and model pinning; we handle migration of routing and caches need time to warm. no heavy rewrite of client code.
[02:51] Olivia: How does billing change during migration? do we double-pay while both sides warm traffic?
[02:57] Liam: Good question. for pilots we recommend a staged cutover: run majority traffic on hosted, a small percentage on dedicated to warm caches. Redwood avoids double billing for identical tokens by deduping at request level when using matched model variants — but some transient extra cost is expected. we'll put numbers in the pricing sheet.
[03:18] [03:18] Ethan: talk through batching — our clients are interactive, so latency SLO is 200–400 ms p95. will batching push latency above that?
[03:27] Priya: There's a tradeoff: synchronous, small-batch requests hit lower latency but higher per-token costs. adaptive continuous batching groups compatible requests within a small window (e.g., 30 ms) which often doesn't break a 200–400 ms SLO and can cut cost substantially for high QPS. we can tune latency budget and batching thresholds per route.
[03:48] Sara: what about KV cache? our conversations often repeat similar prefixes, could that help?
[03:53] Priya: Yes, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as "KV cash" in tooling) stores past key/value attention states for repeated prefixes; for few-shot prompts or long chat histories it can reduce compute. we'd need to measure your prefix repeat rate. if you have common system prompts, you could see 30–70% token savings on the generation path.
[04:12] [04:12] Dr. Patel: Security: SOC 2 is a must. also we use AWS KMS and SAML SSO, and we need audit logs for access. private is preferred if we can't satisfy data residency for PHI-adjacent telemetry.
[04:24] Priya: Redwood supports SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO and KMS integrations. for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. audit logs and per-token request tracing are available in the console. we'll surface the compliance pack in the next email.
[04:41] Olivia: Ok, procurement will need T&Cs and an approx spend forecast.
[04:45] Liam: We'll include a pilot budget model with low/medium/high usage lanes and estimated burn for each host mix.
[04:52] [05:00] Priya: A practical example: if you take an average 420-token roundtrip and we apply a 40% effective caching + batching reduction, your effective billed tokens drop to ~252 tokens. combine with dedicated 40% discount and you can get to the financials Olivia mentioned for pilot. exact numbers depend on model size, quantization, and warm cache hit-rate.
[05:21] Ethan: That math helps. For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[05:25] Priya: - 1k representative requests (redacted), - peak and baseline QPS profile, - desired latency SLOs, - any failure modes to simulate. we'll run the bench in our hosted environment and optionally against dedicated reserve.
[05:36] Sara: timeline for a bench run?
[05:38] Priya: If you can send artifacts in three business days, we can schedule a bench the following week. expect a 90-min SE session plus a short report.
[05:46] [05:46] Olivia: On billing, can you cap spend for the pilot so we don't breach $10k?
[05:50] Liam: Yes, we can implement quota caps and alerts. we'll document guardrails and circuit breaker thresholds for overrun protection.
[05:58] Dr. Patel: How much engineering effort to integrate on our side? minimal is best.
[06:03] Liam: For hosted, integration is simple REST/SDK; for dedicated we provide infra templates and a Redwood operator image; private is heavier and involves networking with your VPC and potentially an on-prem package. we'll include estimated eng hours in the doc.
[06:18] [06:18] Ethan: Any gotchas around token accounting? we sometimes see discrepancy between model tokenizers and client-side counts.
[06:24] Priya: Good point. tokenizer differences can shift counts; we recommend sending canonical tokenized examples. Redwood reports both raw tokens processed and effective billed tokens after caching/dedupe so you'll have visibility.
[06:35] Sara: Are embedding calls billed differently? we plan a vector index for search.
[06:40] Priya: Yes, embeddings are billed per embedding unit. we'll break that out. embedding generation is often cheaper per unit but depends on model.
[06:47] [06:50] Olivia: Procurement question: if we commit to dedicated, what's typical minimum term?
[06:54] Liam: Reserved capacity monthly or annual contracts are common. minimum commitment depends on the pool size; we'll put a small committed pilot option in the pricing sheet with a three-month minimum.
[07:05] Dr. Patel: If we go private eventually, will the tooling still be the same? we want same console/observability.
[07:11] Priya: That's a Redwood design goal: same API and console across hosted/dedicated/private. some advanced ops features like cross-tenant analytics vary by deployment, but routing, tracing, and model pinning remain consistent.
[07:25] [07:25] Ethan: any concerns about model quality when using quantized variants?
[07:29] Priya: There can be small regressions; we do per-model quality profiles and recommend regression tests with your eval set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles that balance cost vs quality.
[07:42] Liam: ok lets wrap with clear next steps. I'll send pricing and pilot tiers. Priya will own bench runs. Ethan and Sara will share a redacted sample and QPS profile. Olivia confirm budget and procurement timeline.
[07:56] Dr. Patel: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:00] Liam: Thanks, we'll follow-up with docs and schedule.

End of transcript. (note: some words or acronyms may be auto-transcribed imperfectly; e.g., "KV cache" sometimes shows as "KV cash" or "VPCe" in early drafts.)
